simple.meaning: צֶלַע (tselaʻ) is a Hebrew word meaning “a limping or full (figuratively).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: צֶלַע (H6761) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 35:15, with occurrences in Psalms, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צֶלַע (H6761) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in צֶלַע (H6761) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: צֶלַע (tselaʻ) / H6761 is traced through Psalms 35:15, Psalms 38:18, Jeremiah 20:10 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6761. tsela צֶ֫לַע noun [masculine] limping, stumbling ; — figurative of calamity, absolute ׳לְצ Psa 38:18 I am ready ( נָכוֺן ) for stumbling (and falling); suffix בְּצַלְעִי 35:15 at my stumbliing ; צ ׳שֹׁמְרֵי Jer 20:10 watchers of my stumbling ; לְצַלְעוֺ נָכוֺן אֵיד Job 18:12 ruin is ready for his stumbling. - See also צֵלָע construct
